summary.headline: Schaeffler India Q1 CY26 revenue rose 18.8% YoY to INR 2,507 crore, with EBITDA of INR 483 crore (19.3% margin) and PAT of INR 319.7 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 18.8% YoY to INR 2,507 crore but fell 5.1% QoQ as management recalibrated the bearings and industrial portfolio and some sectors saw liquidity-driven offtake weakness. EBITDA held at INR 483 crore (19.3% margin, up 18.6% YoY) and PAT rose 12.8% YoY to INR 319.7 crore. Automotive Technologies (+30.8% YoY) and exports (+32.5% YoY) drove growth, while Bearings and Industrial Solutions was up only 4.2% YoY and down 14.3% QoQ. Management flagged supply-chain and fuel-cost pressure from the West Asia crisis, with price recovery expected over about six quarters.

financial_highlights.change: +12.8% YoY per management; marginal drop QoQ
vs INR 237 crore in Q1 CY25; lower QoQ

segments.name: Automotive Technologies
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 30.8% YoY and fell 1.3% QoQ; about 37% of sales. Growth came from ICE clutch and engine systems, with hybrid also strong; new wins in transmission, heavy-duty clutches and hydraulic cam phasers.

segments.name: Bearings and Industrial Solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 4.2% YoY but fell 14.3% QoQ; about 35% of sales. Management cited recalibration, supply-chain disruption and an aftermarket liquidity squeeze; industrial bearings estimated at about 60% localised.

segments.name: Vehicle Lifetime Solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 18.1% YoY and fell 0.6% QoQ; about 12% of sales.

segments.name: Exports (intercompany)
segments.commentary: Grew 32.5% YoY and 6.6% QoQ; about 16% of sales. Management expects CY26 export growth of roughly 10-12%, based on the order book.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue or margin guidance; management said it remains committed to the numbers it has stated.
Management sees no major concern in delivering this year's committed numbers, but says monitoring and agility are required given supply-chain uncertainty.
Export order book for the year shows minimum 10% growth; run-rate full-year export growth of about 10-12%.
Price increases to recover input costs start from Q2; full recovery takes 6-18 months, close to six quarters.
CY26 capex expected in the INR 400-500 crore range, with a pickup from the moderated FY26 level.
Localisation reached about 80% of total revenue; it cannot reach 100% given low initial volumes for new technologies.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex about INR 80 crore (3.1% of sales); management said the moderation was timing-related, not a cut.
CY26 capex guided to INR 400-500 crore, with management targeting about INR 500 crore.
Shoolagiri greenfield plant: transfer of lines from the UK under way, machines arriving, and a second hall being considered; business acquisition needs to be accelerated.
E-axle localisation in Phase 2: setting up the manufacturing line while developing local suppliers for child parts; magnets still imported.
Capacity utilisation at the plant is above 80%, supported by exports.
demand_pricing: Automotive demand strong: about 2.5 million two-wheelers and over 0.5 million cars produced in March 2026 alone, per management.
Bearings: management cited competitive intensity from local capacity build-out, leading to pricing pressure and a portfolio recalibration at the start of the year.

Aftermarket industrial demand slowed because of a liquidity crunch at distributors, with a seasonal Q1 effect that management expects to reverse next quarter. Railways and power transmission were described as stable to good; mining was weak.

Fuel and LPG costs rose after West Asia supply disruption; mitigation via alternate sourcing, stockpiling and seeking customer compensation. Too early to quantify (about 1.5 months since the increase).
Exports are mainly to group companies in Europe, China, Southeast Asia and the Americas; management sees no demand dip.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CY26 outlook for industrial segments such as wind, railways and off-road?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no major concerns in delivering this year's committed numbers, though supply-chain uncertainty from the Middle East requires daily crisis management meetings.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly 31% Automotive Technologies growth, well above underlying production growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Strong traction across ICE, hybrid and e-mobility platforms; almost all ICE product lines grew strongly in Q1, and management expects the automotive trend to stay robust.

qa_highlights.question: Why did bearings stay flat to down, and is demand or competition the cause?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited localisation, product and market mix recalibration, rising competitor activity and pricing pressure, plus an aftermarket liquidity squeeze; it said the recalibration was done at the start of the year.

qa_highlights.question: How are the export geographies performing?
qa_highlights.answer: Europe, China, Southeast Asia and the Americas are all stable with no demand dip; the order book shows at least 10% growth for the year.

qa_highlights.question: How long does it take to pass on input cost increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases begin in Q2; full recovery takes 6-18 months, close to six quarters, under the price-excellence mechanism.

qa_highlights.question: Is inventory building up at quarter end?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, there was an inventory buildup in the quarter; management expects better inventory levels in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 2026 capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 400-500 crore in CY26, with a pickup toward about INR 500 crore after the FY25 rationalisation.

risks_watch: Middle East and West Asia supply-chain disruption and fuel/LPG cost inflation, with uncertain recovery from customers.
Bearings and industrial margin pressure from local competition and pricing; watch Q2 for whether aftermarket liquidity normalises as management expects.
Export growth is dependent on intercompany orders, and the full-year run rate has been cut to about 10-12%.
Liquidity pressure on distributors and customers affecting cash flow (FCF fell to INR 137 crore from INR 237 crore YoY).
KRSV remains loss-making (EBITDA -13.4%), dragging consolidated results.
E-axle competition (for example, Tata-Bosch JV) and the pace of Phase 2 localisation and supplier development.
summary.management_tone: Confident on automotive, exports and the margin base, but cautious and somewhat evasive on bearings and industrial weakness, which management attributed to several causes. Management repeatedly stressed that the Q1 issues were partly seasonal and that it would not give formal guidance.
key_quotes: We do not see major concerns in terms of delivering the numbers that we are committed to deliver this year.
It takes somewhere between six months to 18 months to have the full recovery.
It can never be 100%, in my opinion, as the technologies evolve, initial volumes, for example, e-axle initial volumes are lower.

growth.why: No formal revenue or margin guidance; management reiterated commitment to stated numbers, with export order book showing minimum 10% growth for CY26 and CY26 capex of INR 400-500 crore, though domestic bearings softened and price recovery takes about six quarters.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: from Q2 FY27 onward, full recovery over ~6 quarters
rows.why: EBITDA margin held at 19.3% in the quarter, and price increases to recover input costs start in Q2, but fuel/LPG cost inflation from West Asia is not yet quantified and bearings face pricing pressure from local competitors.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Shoolagiri greenfield plant has lines transferred from the UK and machines arriving with a second hall under consideration, while utilisation is above 80%, though timing of commissioning was not specified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Export order book shows minimum 10% growth for CY26 (run-rate 10-12%), and Automotive Technologies grew 30.8% YoY, though Bearings and Industrial grew only 4.2% YoY and fell 14.3% QoQ.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is above 80% and CY26 capex is guided to INR 400-500 crore (targeting about INR 500 crore), a pickup from the moderated Q1 level of about INR 80 crore.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management issues no formal revenue or margin guidance and said only that it is committed to delivering stated numbers; bearings and industrial softness and the cut to export growth to 10-12% argue against an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Bearings revenue fell 14.3% QoQ, FCF dropped to INR 137 crore from INR 237 crore YoY, and West Asia supply and fuel cost impacts are not yet quantified, though management sees no major concern in delivering committed numbers.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New wins in transmission, heavy-duty clutches and hydraulic cam phasers were mentioned, and E-axle Phase 2 line is being set up, but no specific launch dates were given.

rows.label: KRSV Innovative Auto Solutions reaching breakeven
rows.why: KRSV revenue is INR 78.7 crore with EBITDA of -13.4% and is described as not yet breakeven, with no timeline given.

rows.label: Inventory normalisation and aftermarket liquidity recovery
rows.why: Management expects the Q1 aftermarket seasonal effect to reverse next quarter and better inventory levels in coming quarters, though working capital stands at 17.9% of sales and FCF fell to INR 137 crore.

rows.label: Input cost price recovery via price-excellence mechanism
rows.when: from Q2 FY27, full recovery in ~6 quarters
rows.why: Price increases start in Q2 with full recovery taking 6-18 months, which supports margins against fuel and supply-chain cost inflation.

tone.note: Management was confident on automotive, exports and the margin base and committed to stated numbers, but cautious and somewhat evasive on bearings and industrial weakness; analysts pressed on bearings demand versus competition and the West Asia supply-chain impact.
